summary.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 819 stores in 559 cities at June 2026 end after 27 openings in the quarter, including 10 in South India; total trading area 13.8 million sq ft.

segments.name: Small format
segments.commentary: 3 small stores opened in the quarter (16 in total cited); currently run only in UP and Haryana, with a stated opportunity of about 3,000 small-format stores nationally.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: Contributed 75.2% of revenue; 100% of apparel, about 75% of general merchandise, about 60% by volume of FMCG, and about 50% of kitchen appliances (Tandem brand).

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: 767 stores across 520 cities and over 1.4 crore registered consumers; contributes 2-9% of store revenue, at least 5% in most locations; average bill about INR 800; 20% of customers are new to Vishal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper in subsequent quarters.
Small-format stores to accelerate; current guidance cited as 80 to 100 small-format store additions.
RFID rollout: Delhi NCR stores live; full network rollout expected to slightly exceed one year.
No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.
Gross margin sustainability depends on current cost structure; management says no significant issue if circumstances hold, but declined to forecast West Asia-linked developments.
Foreign ownership to be capped at 49.99% to keep the company Indian owned and controlled; foreign holding is close to 20% today.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 27 in Q1 FY27 (819 total); small-format openings were slow at 3 in the quarter, with some large-format stores opened alongside.
New format: first pilot store said to be very close to launch, followed by one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision.
RFID: pilot in 2 stores in Delhi NCR, now extended to all Delhi NCR stores; stock counts possible in 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts.
Minimum wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others lifted employee cost per sq ft about 13% YoY.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Price increases were limited to higher price points and selected categories; opening and mid price points were not raised, and price-sensitive categories such as children's clothing and staple foods were left unchanged.
Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory was INR 1,900 crore. The new format is near its first pilot store launch, with one or two more pilots planned before a roll-out decision.

risks_watch: Elevated inflation weighing on demand; management expects easing but gave no firm timeline.
Gross margin sustainability: the gain depends on lower promotions and holding prices; West Asia developments are an open risk.
Structural rise in employee costs from minimum wage increases across several states.
Competitive pressure in apparel from value retailers; management says the competitor set is unchanged, but pace is a watch item.
Leadership change: COO Manoj departs and Sashi Gumma replaces him; further org changes not discussed.
Small-format and RFID roll-outs are gradual; timing and benefits remain to be proven at scale.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margins, with clear caveats: management avoided forecasting macro or West Asia impacts, said forward gross margin is conditional on current cost structure, and gave no firm dates for the new format or small-format scale-up. Several analyst questions were lost to audio issues and management answered some only partially.
key_quotes: Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crores, which was a growth of 19.3% over last year, and our operating margin (Operating EBITDA margin) improved from 10.3% last year to 10.4% this year.
The fact is that the small format is half the size of a regular format.
But I'm not saying that I can see the future any better than any of us on the West Asia crisis and so on.
Under no circumstances, would we allow a price discount to the market leader become lesser than before.

adds.what: 27 store openings in Q1 FY27 (819 total, 559 cities); small-format stores 3 opened in quarter, 80-100 small-format additions guided
New format: first pilot store very close to launch, followed by 1-2 more pilots before roll-out decision

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper, 80-100 small-format additions guided, and 27 stores added in Q1 with 10% SSG, so growth is supported by store additions and demand but not quantified for the year.
